correctness.rationale: The finite model and its full law follow from the union-of-intact-cycles lemma, with the shared hub counted once; independent site retention yields the intersection probability p^(a+b-1). The strict nonempty-core order is an exact positive factorization. In the mean comparison, Descartes' rule and a simple endpoint root give one and only one interior crossing; the n=11 minimality follows by listing even cycle length partitions. An independent standard-library enumerator exactly checks the full output-law Bernstein coefficients for 119424 retention subsets in nine graphs. Infinite parameter conclusions are analytical.

value.rationale: The theorem separates the ecologically different targets probability of retaining any two-neighbor-supported mutualistic core and expected species richness of that core. It fixes the full degree distributions inside both ecological guilds while proving that each balancing transfer universally decreases nonempty probability yet changes the expected-size ranking exactly once. The first feasible 11-species network pair has an exact threshold 1/sqrt(2). The structure applies to all even cycle length pairs in this biologically motivated family; it is not an arbitrary invariant census and makes no unsupported empirical claims.
